proof.text: For an etale covering $\{W_i\to W\}$ in $Y_{\Et}$, put $W_a=W\times_Y Y_a$ and $W_{i,a}=W_i\times_Y Y_a$. The maps $W_{i,a}\to W_a$ are again a jointly surjective etale family. A matching family in $E(W_i)$ is exactly, for each $a$, a matching family in $\underline{M_a}(W_{i,a})$. Glue each such family uniquely in $\underline{M_a}(W_a)$ and take the tuple. This proves the sheaf axiom for the displayed formula, including the empty covering: a module sheaf has the zero module on the empty scheme. Define the action of $\lambda\in\Lambda_Y(W)$ on a tuple $(s_a)_a$ by $(\lambda|_{W_a}s_a)_a$. The module identities and semilinearity of restrictions hold componentwise, so $E$ is a sheaf of $\Lambda_Y$-modules.

source.place: Second paragraph, finite product of the constant sheaves on the normalizations; explicit sheaf construction on their disjoint union.

proof.text: Write $\iota_a:Y_a\hookrightarrow Y$ for a coprojection. It is an open immersion by the disjoint-union hypothesis, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. For $W\to Y_a$ etale, viewed as an object over $Y$, disjointness gives $W\times_Y Y_b=\varnothing$ for $b\ne a$ and $W\times_Y Y_a\cong W$. Thus projection to the $a$th factor is an isomorphism $E(W)\cong\underline{M_a}(W)$, inverse to inserting zero in the other factors. These maps commute with every restriction and with the restricted coefficient action. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction](1), inverse image of the underlying abelian sheaf along the etale map $\iota_a$ is restriction to these objects. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-inverse-image-comparison] this is also the underlying abelian sheaf of the fixed-coefficient module inverse image. The comparison is determined by the adjunction unit; its maps on germs commute with multiplication by each $\lambda\in\Lambda$, and hence with local sections of the constant ring sheaf, which are locally represented by such $\lambda$. Consequently the projection above gives the required module isomorphism $\iota_a^{-1}E\cong\underline{M_a}_{Y_a}$.

The coprojection is etale by morphisms.tex, Tag 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale).

proof.text: The finitely many images $|Y_a|$ cover $|Y|$, are pairwise disjoint, and are locally closed because they are clopen; the maps $\iota_a$ realize them as immersed subschemes. This is the stratification of [def-constructible-stratification]. Each $|Y_a|$ is also retrocompact: for a quasi-compact open $U\subseteq Y$, an open cover of $U\cap Y_a$, together with $U\setminus Y_a$, covers $U$ and has a finite subcover; the selected members cover $U\cap Y_a$. Thus $Y_a$ is open and retrocompact. The empty open is retrocompact, so $|Y_a|=|Y_a|\cap(Y\setminus\varnothing)$ is a constructible subset by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. This argument uses no Noetherian or quasi-compact assumption on $Y$.

proof.text: On each $Y_a$, step 2 exhibits $\iota_a^{-1}E$ as the constant module sheaf with the finite value $M_a$. The identity cover of $Y_a$ is therefore a finite-value trivialization. Apply implication (1)$\Rightarrow$(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values], with base $Y_a$, coefficient ring $\Lambda$, and sheaf $\iota_a^{-1}E$: it is finite locally constant in the coefficient category of $\Lambda$-modules, including finiteness of every geometric stalk. Its further assertion identifies those stalks with $M_a$. In particular the finite-value formulation and the finite-stalk formulation used in the two constructibility definitions both hold.

proof.text: Use the single finite clopen stratification from step 3. Its strata are constructible, and the module restrictions have finite constant models by step 2. These are exactly conditions (a) and (b) of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Thus it witnesses the first constructibility assertion. By step 4 the same restrictions are finite locally constant in the coefficient category of $\Lambda$-modules, so the same stratification also witnesses [def-constructible-constructible]. Empty components may be omitted. If $r=0$, then $Y=\varnothing$, $E$ is the zero sheaf given by the empty product, and the empty stratification satisfies both definitions vacuously.

title: Componentwise finite constant sheaves on a finite clopen union are constructible
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, let $Y=\coprod_{a=1}^rY_a$ be a finite disjoint union of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with each $Y_a$ open and closed in $Y$, and let $M_a$ be a finite $\Lambda$-module, with constant sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Define a sheaf of $\Lambda_Y$-modules $E$ on the small etale site of $Y$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], as a module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] by
$$E(W)=\prod_{a=1}^r\underline{M_a}_{Y_a}(W\times_Y Y_a)$$
for every etale $W\to Y$, with componentwise restrictions and module operations. Then the clopen partition $Y=\coprod_aY_a$, together with the constant finite module restriction $E|_{Y_a}\cong\underline{M_a}_{Y_a}$, is a constructibility stratification [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]; in particular $E$ is constructible as a $\Lambda$-module sheaf in that sense and also in [def-constructible-constructible] for the coefficient category of $\Lambda$-modules.
